sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the north-western corner of Haddon Heights, along the Audubon borough line, and is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the long axis of the streets running down the page; north points to the upper right. The Kings Highway crosses the top of the sheet on the diagonal, lettered as the Borough of Audubon line, and the Atlantic City Railroad (P. & R. Ry.) runs down the middle of the sheet between West Atlantic Avenue on the left and East Atlantic Avenue on the right. 7th Avenue forms the left edge and the Whitehorse Pike, also lettered 5th Avenue, the right edge. Green crosses the sheet at about two thirds of its height, dividing the upper blocks from the lower ones, and the bottom edge is a match line to sheet 4. The upper right block holds the Haddon Heights Public School, a large pink brick building lettered with heat by steam and electric lights, and St. Mary's Church Episcl., a stone dwelling-sized church building with its lots; the other buildings are almost all frame dwellings with their rear sheds, drawn in yellow with a few stone or brick-veneered houses in blue. Lots are numbered along the street fronts, with block numbers 31, 32, 41 and 42. Near the railroad at Green a watch box and a signal tower are shown. Water mains of 4, 6 and 8 inches are drawn in the streets, with hydrants at the corners and fire alarm boxes at Green and the Pike.
notes: Drawn at 50 feet to an inch (scale bar on the sheet); north points to the upper right (fitted rotation about 40 degrees).
Green is today Green Street and Whitehorse Pike is White Horse Pike (OpenStreetMap).
A line of lettering along the Kings Highway reads like 'Cong Bridge' next to 'Borough Line'; it could not be read with confidence and is not listed as a street.
50 ft. NW corner: Kings Highway (Audubon line) to Green; 7th Av to White Horse Pike; Atlantic City RR with W/E Atlantic Av.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 lies east of sheet 2 and is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, turned like its neighbours so that north points to the upper right. The Whitehorse Pike, also lettered 5th Avenue, forms the left edge and 3rd Avenue the right edge, with 4th Avenue running down the middle. The Kings Highway crosses the upper part of the sheet on the diagonal, marked as the Borough of Audubon line, with Amherst Road leaving it on the north side near the top right. Green crosses the sheet at about the height of three fifths and separates the upper blocks from the lower ones; the bottom edge is a match line to sheet 5. The upper right block is occupied by a church group: St. Rose of Lima R.C. Church with a spire, a hall, and the St. Rose Parochial School, a pink brick building with an auditorium and stage, all with heat by steam and electric lights. The rest of the sheet is residential, frame dwellings with rear sheds and a few stone or brick-veneered houses, with several vacant lots in the upper left block and a small office at the corner of the Pike and Kings Highway. Block numbers 18, 19, 29 and 30 are shown. Water mains of 4, 6 and 8 inches run in the streets with hydrants at the corners, and a compass rose stands at the top of the sheet.
notes: Drawn at 50 feet to an inch (scale bar on the sheet); fitted rotation about 40 degrees.
Green is today Green Street and Whitehorse Pike is White Horse Pike (OpenStreetMap).
50 ft. White Horse Pike to 3rd Av, 4th Av; Kings Highway to Green; St. Rose church and school.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 shows the business centre of Haddon Heights at the railroad station, at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. The Atlantic City Railroad (P. & R. Ry.) runs down the middle of the sheet with West Atlantic Avenue on its west side and East Atlantic Avenue on its east side. 7th Avenue forms the left edge and the Whitehorse Pike, also lettered 5th Avenue, the right edge. Station Avenue crosses at about two fifths of the sheet height and Garden runs along the bottom, with a match line to sheet 2 at the top. On the west side of the tracks stand the Post Office, the public library with borough offices, borough hall and Masonic hall in one building, the Fire Dept (built 1925), a row of stores with tin clad bays, the Friesland Apts, plumbers and sheet metal shops, Ramsay's Garage, a printing shop and the Haddon Heights Lumber Co. yard with a long lumber shed and a siding from the main line. The Passenger Station and a freight house stand beside the tracks. East of the tracks are the Central Garage of Evaul Bros. with a second garage, rows of stores along the Pike, and the Haddon Heights Bank & Trust Co. (built 1925). Rows of brick and tile-wall dwellings fill the south west blocks and frame houses the south east ones.
notes: Drawn at 50 feet to an inch (scale bar on the sheet); fitted rotation about 40 degrees.
Station Avenue and Garden are today Station Avenue and Garden Street; Whitehorse Pike is White Horse Pike (OpenStreetMap).
The railroad is the line now shown in OpenStreetMap as the Beesleys Point Secondary and Atlantic City Line, next to East and West Atlantic Avenue.
Junctions with Garden Street at the bottom edge are hand-picked (the street centre lies at or beyond the edge of the scan).
50 ft. Station area: Station Av to Garden; 7th Av to White Horse Pike; railroad, W/E Atlantic Av, post office, fire dept. Garden St row hand-picked at the bottom edge.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 lies south of sheet 3, between the Whitehorse Pike (also lettered 5th Avenue) on the left and 3rd Avenue on the right, with 4th Avenue down the middle. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Station Avenue crosses the sheet at about two fifths of its height, and Garden runs along the bottom edge; the top edge is a match line to sheet 3. The upper left block holds the Haddon Heights Baptist Church, a frame building with a tower and heat by steam and electric lights, and the upper right block the 1st Church of Christ Scientist, with the foundation of an addition marked beside it. The remaining blocks are residential: frame dwellings with rear sheds in regular lots, a few stone or brick-veneered houses and some concrete-block outbuildings, two greenhouses in the lower left block, and a number of vacant lots. Block numbers 19, 20, 28 and 29 are given, and lot numbers are written along the street fronts. Water mains of 4 and 6 inches run in the streets, with hydrants at the corners and a fire alarm box at Garden. A compass rose is drawn in the middle of the upper left block, and the scale bar stands at the foot of the sheet.
notes: Drawn at 50 feet to an inch (scale bar on the sheet); fitted rotation about 40 degrees.
Station Avenue and Garden are today Station Avenue and Garden Street; Whitehorse Pike is White Horse Pike (OpenStreetMap).
50 ft. White Horse Pike to 3rd Av, Station Av to Garden.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the eastern edge of the built-up part of Haddon Heights, between 3rd Avenue on the left and the Haddonfield borough line on the right, and is drawn at 100 feet to an inch (scale note on the sheet) with north toward the upper right. 3rd, 2nd and 1st Avenues run down the page and Crest Avenue and Lippincott Avenue close the east side, crossed by Garden at the bottom, Station Avenue in the middle and the Kings Highway along the top on the diagonal, lettered as the Borough of Audubon line. Westmont Road and Brick Kiln Road leave the Kings Highway on its north side. Loucroft Avenue crosses the upper right. The west half is closely built with frame dwellings and rear sheds, numbered along the street fronts, with a few brick and stone houses. The area between 1st Avenue and Lippincott Avenue is mostly vacant, with a few buildings on the edge, and the right-hand part beyond the Borough of Haddonfield line is blank paper, with a large open block lettered 1, 2, 3 and 4 and some stand pipes. The sheet carries block numbers 1 to 11 and 16 and 17, 6 inch water mains in Station Avenue and the cross streets, and 8 and 10 inch mains along the Kings Highway. Sheets 3, 5 and 7 adjoin on the left, below left and at the foot.
notes: Drawn at 100 feet to an inch (scale bar on the sheet); fitted rotation about 40 degrees. Sheets 2 to 5 are at 50 feet.
Westmont Road meets the Kings Highway where OpenStreetMap has Crystal Lake Avenue (identification not checked on the ground). Brick Kiln Road is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Station Avenue and Garden are today Station Avenue and Garden Street.
Garden is lettered at two places, offset from each other, at the bottom left and at the foot of 1st Avenue.
100 ft. 3rd Av to Haddonfield line, Kings Highway to Garden; Crest, Lippincott, Loucroft Avs.

sheet-7-1.description: The main part of sheet 7 shows the southeastern corner of Haddon Heights between Garden Street at the top and Highland Avenue, the line with Centre Township, along the lower edge of the part. Third, Second and First Avenues run down the page, with Crest Avenue to the right; Garden Street and High Street cross them and both jog at First and Second Avenues. The left half is a residential district of long lots with frame dwellings and private garages facing Third and Second Avenues. Between Second and First Avenues, Haddon Heights High School occupies the block below Garden Street: a large building of concrete and brick with an auditorium and gymnasium, noted as built in 1923, with a large athletic field behind it. The blocks between First and Crest Avenues are partly built with dwellings, and beyond Crest Avenue the part reaches open ground at the Borough of Haddonfield line, drawn as a dash-dot line running up to the top of the sheet. Haddon Avenue and High Street are lettered at the left edge where they meet Third Avenue. A heavy line along Highland Avenue separates this part from two smaller parts at the bottom of the sheet that show other places. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches and hydrants are marked in the streets. Sheet 6 adjoins at the top and sheet 8 at the left.
notes: Highland Avenue along the Centre Township line is today Clements Bridge Road; Haddon Avenue at Third Avenue is Haddon Street; Garden is Garden Street and High is East High Street (OpenStreetMap).
Haddon Heights High School, built 1923, with an athletic field.

100 ft. Three parts separated by heavy lines: 1 main (3rd, 2nd, 1st, Crest Avs, Garden to Highland Av = Clements Bridge Road; High School); 2 outline of Bellmawr Av at Cedar/Pine/Chestnut by Little Timber Creek (repeats sheets 12/13; helmert from 2 points); 3 E. Atlantic Av to White Horse Pike at Highland Av, Barrington line (anchored on a point carried from sheet 8 plus a derived point, low confidence).

sheet-7-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 7 is a small outline drawing in the triangle between the two heavy lines at the right of the sheet. It shows Bellmawr Avenue running diagonally up the page with short ends of Cedar Avenue and Chestnut Avenue on its west side, Pine Avenue at the bottom and Maple Street at the right edge, with Little Timber Creek and the line of the Borough of Barrington crossing the lower part. No buildings are drawn: the blocks are marked with the numbers 13 and 12 of the sheets that show them in full, and the large lot 70 of sheet 12 lies south of Pine Avenue. A dash-dot match line lettered A and B on the right joins the left edge of sheet 12. This is the southern end of Bellmawr Avenue near the creek, about a kilometre and a half west of the main part of the sheet. A north arrow is drawn at the right.
notes: Outline only; the area is drawn in detail on sheets 12 and 13.
Pine Avenue is not in the OpenStreetMap extract; the part is placed from Bellmawr Avenue at Cedar Avenue (detected) and at the west branch of Chestnut Avenue (hand-picked), a two-point helmert fit.

100 ft. Three parts separated by heavy lines: 1 main (3rd, 2nd, 1st, Crest Avs, Garden to Highland Av = Clements Bridge Road; High School); 2 outline of Bellmawr Av at Cedar/Pine/Chestnut by Little Timber Creek (repeats sheets 12/13; helmert from 2 points); 3 E. Atlantic Av to White Horse Pike at Highland Av, Barrington line (anchored on a point carried from sheet 8 plus a derived point, low confidence).

sheet-7-3.description: Part 3 of sheet 7 fills the lower left of the sheet below the heavy lines and shows a place on the Barrington line south of the main part: East Atlantic Avenue and White Horse Pike, also lettered 5th Avenue, running down the page to Highland Avenue, which crosses the bottom of the part as the Borough of Barrington line. The railroad tracks lettered A.C.R.R. and P.R.R. run beside East Atlantic Avenue at the left, with the Barrington borough line. Between the two avenues are the H. M. Krebs coal yard with sheds and an office, a few dwellings, and a farm group with a wagon shed, coops and a dwelling; a small stream crosses the part from top to bottom and passes under Highland Avenue. On White Horse Pike at Highland Avenue stands a garage with a capacity of 30 cars and a gasoline filling station. A dash-dot match line lettered A and B crosses the part. A separate north arrow is drawn at the lower right.
notes: Highland Avenue here is today Clements Bridge Road; the modern junction with White Horse Pike has been rebuilt with ramps.
H. M. Krebs coal yard; garage for 30 cars on White Horse Pike.

Placed from one point carried from sheet 8 (White Horse Pike on the A-B match line) and a derived point at sheet 8 scale and rotation: low confidence. The modern junction of White Horse Pike and Clements Bridge Road gave a rotation 6 degrees off and was dropped.

100 ft. Three parts separated by heavy lines: 1 main (3rd, 2nd, 1st, Crest Avs, Garden to Highland Av = Clements Bridge Road; High School); 2 outline of Bellmawr Av at Cedar/Pine/Chestnut by Little Timber Creek (repeats sheets 12/13; helmert from 2 points); 3 E. Atlantic Av to White Horse Pike at Highland Av, Barrington line (anchored on a point carried from sheet 8 plus a derived point, low confidence).

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the central business and residential core of Haddon Heights, from Garden Street at the top of the page to Highland Avenue, the line with the Borough of Barrington and Centre Township, at the bottom. The White Horse Pike, lettered also as 5th Avenue, runs down the middle of the sheet, with 4th Avenue and 3rd Avenue parallel to it on the right. Haddon Avenue and High Street cross them, and Grove Street cuts across the lower left. Between 5th and 3rd Avenues the blocks, numbered 21 to 27, are closely built with frame dwellings, many with private garages, and the blocks below Haddon Avenue (23 to 25) continue the same pattern as far as Highland Avenue. A Haddon garage with its cement floor and steam heat stands on the pike at Haddon Avenue, and the Evangelical Lutheran Church of the Ascension stands in the lower blocks. To the left of the pike, the double tracks of the Atlantic City Railroad run diagonally down the page, with East Atlantic Avenue along their east side and West Atlantic Avenue along the west. Beyond the tracks lie the top-left blocks 44 to 46 with rows of brick semi-detached houses on Sycamore Terrace and West High Street, a ball ground, and the auxiliary pumping station of the New Jersey Water Company with its pump house. At the foot of the left side a Public Service Corporation electric substation with open transformers stands near Grove Street, and Little Timber Creek winds along the lower left corner on the line with Barrington. Four-inch and six-inch water mains are shown in every street. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right.
notes: Highland Avenue, the Barrington and Centre Township line, is today Clements Bridge Road (OpenStreetMap).
Haddon Avenue is today Haddon Street; High is East High Street east of the pike and West High Street west of it; Grove is today Grove Street; Garden is today Garden Street (OpenStreetMap).
Whitehorse Pike, also lettered 5th Avenue, is today White Horse Pike.

100 ft. Central core: Garden to Highland Av (Clements Bridge Road), White Horse Pike (5th Av), 3rd/4th Avs, Haddon Av, Grove; West Atlantic/Sycamore Ter. blocks top left; Atlantic City RR down the left. Atlantic Avenues left out (rail).

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers the western residential district of Haddon Heights between Station Avenue at the top and Little Timber Creek, the line with the Borough of Barrington, at the bottom. The numbered avenues 7th, 8th, 9th, 10th and 11th run down the page, crossed by Station Avenue, Garden and W. High, while in the upper left South Park Avenue, Lake, Prospect Ridge Avenue and Sycamore run diagonally across the sheet at an angle to the grid, with long narrow lots between them. Most of the blocks (numbered 48 to 59) are closely built with frame dwellings and private garages; the lower blocks 56, 57 and 68 are only partly built, with scattered houses on large unsubdivided tracts. Near the right edge the First M. E. Church stands on Garden at 7th Avenue, with the public school, heated by hot air and lit by electricity, a block south of it. Water mains of 4 and 6 inches run in every street with hydrants at the corners and several fire alarm boxes. The lower right corner is blank, holding the compass and scale, and 8th Avenue is marked not opened below W. High. Little Timber Creek meanders along the bottom, marked as the borough line. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right.
notes: Prospect Ridge Avenue is today Prospect Ridge Boulevard; Sycamore, Lake, Garden, West High and South Park Avenue are today Sycamore Street, Lake Street, Garden Street, West High Street and South Park Avenue (OpenStreetMap).
Sycamore Ter at the right edge continues on sheet 8, where it is lettered Sycamore Ter.; today Sycamore Terrace.
8th Avenue is marked not opened south of West High.
100 ft. 7th to 11th Avs, Station Av to Little Timber Creek; diagonal S. Park / Lake / Prospect Ridge / Sycamore at upper left.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers the northwestern part of Haddon Heights, from Kings Highway, the borough line with Audubon, along the top of the page to Station Avenue at the foot. The numbered avenues 7th to 11th run down the page, crossed by Green about a third of the way from the bottom, so that the long blocks above it (numbers 51, 52, 61 and 62) are lined with small frame dwellings on narrow lots facing the avenues, and the blocks below it (50, 53, 60 and 63) are almost as closely built. A few buildings along Kings Highway are larger, including a group of connected buildings with a blue-coloured roof on 10th Avenue and a pink brick building at the upper right. The First Presbyterian Church, heated by steam and lighted by electricity, stands on the block at 7th Avenue above Green, and a greenhouse with potting house stands at 8th Avenue below it. At the lower left North Park Avenue and South Park Avenue run diagonally on either side of a long narrow lake lettered Lake and Borough Property, and 11th Avenue is marked not open where it meets the lake. Glover Avenue appears at the upper left, curving through unbuilt ground. Water mains of 4 and 6 inches are shown in all streets, with hydrants, and the 12-inch main runs along Kings Highway. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right.
notes: Green is today Green Street; Lake St. is today Lake Street (OpenStreetMap).
11th Avenue is marked not open below Green, at the lake.
Kings Highway is drawn as the borough line with Audubon; its 10th Avenue junction was rejected as 19 m off the fit.
The lake between North and South Park Avenues is lettered "Lake" and "Borough Property".
100 ft. Kings Highway (Audubon line) to Station Av, 7th to 11th Avs, Green; Borough Lake and N./S. Park Avs lower left.

sheet-11-1.description: The main part of sheet 11 covers the northwestern edge of Haddon Heights along Kings Highway, the line with the Borough of Audubon, which crosses the top of the sheet. At the upper left are the blocks of Keswick and Sylvan Avenues between Line Street and 13th Avenue, closely subdivided into narrow lots with frame dwellings. Edgewood Street and a road run north from Kings Highway into Audubon, and Cedarcroft Avenue is lettered at the upper right. On the south side of the highway a row of dwellings faces McAloon Avenue, and down the right side runs Glover Avenue with the lots of the Kings Highway Section Plan No. 2 between it and 11th Avenue, which curves up to the highway. The centre of the sheet is open ground crossed by the South Branch of Newton Creek, with the Haddon Heights Sewage Disposal Plant and its filter beds beside the creek and a road leading to it. At the bottom are the ends of Prospect Ridge Boulevard, Bellmawr Avenue and South Park Avenue, Green Street, and 11th Avenue marked not opened, with North Park Avenue at the corner. A heavy line separates a second part at the lower left, which shows Kings Highway further west. Water pipes and hydrants are marked; neighbouring sheets 10, 12, 13 and 15 are referenced at the edges.
notes: Line is today Dallas Avenue; Edgewood Street is Edgewood Avenue; Sylvan Avenue is Sylvan Drive; McAloon is probably Thornolden Avenue (OpenStreetMap).
Haddon Heights Sewage Disposal Plant on the South Branch of Newton Creek.
11th Avenue south of Green is marked not opened.
McAloon is lettered with the word "arbitrary" under it (the street index lists "McAloon (arbitrary)"), a name assigned by the mapmaker.

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main (Kings Highway on the Audubon line, Keswick/Sylvan/13th, Glover Av, sewage disposal plant, Newton Creek); 2 lower left, Kings Highway from Hampshire St to Line (Dallas Av), drawn displaced at the same rotation (4 points incl. 1 hand-picked, low confidence).

sheet-11-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 11, separated from the main part by a heavy line at the lower left of the sheet, shows Kings Highway between Hampshire Street and Line Street, the Borough of Audubon line, and the land west of Line Street down to the South Branch of Newton Creek. Kings Highway runs diagonally from the upper left, with a 12 inch water pipe, and Line Street runs down from it to Keswick Avenue and Sylvan Avenue, whose ends are drawn east of it with a few lots. Most of the part is open land in two large lots numbered 78 and 79, bordered on the left by the winding South Branch of Newton Creek. Buildings are few: the Supplee-Wills-Jones distributing station near Hampshire Street, a dwelling on the highway, and a small New Jersey Water Company pumping station near Sylvan Avenue. The part overlaps the left edge of the main part along Line Street and is drawn at the same orientation, displaced on the page to fit. A north arrow is drawn in the part. Sheet 15 adjoins at the left.
notes: Line is today Dallas Avenue, Hampshire Street is Hampshire Avenue and Sylvan Avenue is Sylvan Drive (OpenStreetMap).
Supplee-Wills-Jones distributing station; New Jersey Water Company pumping station.
Placed from three detected junctions along Line Street and one hand-picked point at Hampshire Street: low confidence.

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main (Kings Highway on the Audubon line, Keswick/Sylvan/13th, Glover Av, sewage disposal plant, Newton Creek); 2 lower left, Kings Highway from Hampshire St to Line (Dallas Av), drawn displaced at the same rotation (4 points incl. 1 hand-picked, low confidence).

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 shows the southwestern residential district of Haddon Heights around Lake Street, between Bell Mawr Avenue on the west and Prospect Ridge and South Park Avenues on the north, down to Little Timber Creek, the line with the Borough of Barrington, at the lower left. The street grid is drawn at an angle, with north toward the upper right. Lake Street runs diagonally across the middle of the sheet and jogs at Sycamore Street and again at West High Street, as it still does today; Sycamore and West High Street cross it from upper left to lower right, and short ends of Sycamore Street, West High Street, Maple Avenue and Oak Avenue are drawn west of Bell Mawr Avenue where they are offset. The blocks between Bell Mawr Avenue and Lake Street are lined with long narrow lots holding frame dwellings with private garages; the blocks along Prospect Ridge Avenue and South Park Avenue toward the lake at the top right are more fully built. South of West High Street the sheet is mostly open land: large lots numbered 69, 69A, 69B and 70, crossed by 13th, 12th and 11th Avenues, with a row of houses on 11th Avenue at the lower right. A sewage pumping station stands near Lake Street by Little Timber Creek. A dash-dot match line lettered A and B along the left edge joins the area drawn on sheet 7. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches and hydrants are marked in most streets. Neighbouring sheets 7, 9, 10, 11 and 13 are referenced at the edges.
notes: Bell Mawr Avenue is today Bellmawr Avenue; Prospect Ridge Avenue is Prospect Ridge Boulevard; Lake is Lake Street (OpenStreetMap).
Lake Street, Sycamore Street, West High Street and Maple Avenue are drawn with the same jogs at Bell Mawr Avenue and Lake Street that they have today.
Sewage pumping station by Little Timber Creek.
100 ft. Lake St district: Bell Mawr Av to Prospect Ridge/S. Park Avs, down to Little Timber Creek. Lake, Sycamore, W. High jog as today. Lake St / Maple Av excluded (misleads the fit).

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 covers the western edge of Haddon Heights, a large newly platted tract laid out in regular rectangular blocks between Prospect Ridge Boulevard at the top of the page and Hazel Avenue at the foot, and between Glenview Avenue on the left and Bellmawr Avenue on the right. Sycamore, W. High, Maple Avenue, Oak Avenue, Chestnut Avenue, Cedar Avenue and Pine Avenue cross the sheet from side to side, with Devon Avenue and Glenside Avenue running down the page between Glenview and Bellmawr. Every block is divided into long narrow building lots, numbered with older block numbers in parentheses (blocks 130 to 167), but almost none are built on: a few scattered frame dwellings and garages stand on the blocks in the upper right and near Devon and Oak Avenues, and Bethany Presbyterian Church, heated by hot air and lighted by electricity, stands on block 130 at the upper left. In the upper left corner Hillside Avenue crosses the sheet at an angle, and the blocks beside it are laid out diagonally. Water mains of 4 and 6 inches run in Sycamore, W. High and Maple Avenue. A narrow strip down the right edge, with Sycamore Street, W. High Street and Maple Avenue lettered across it, belongs to the district drawn on sheet 12. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and is turned only slightly from the compass, with north toward the top of the page.
notes: Sycamore is today Sycamore Street and W. High is West High Street; Prospect Ridge Blvd. is today Prospect Ridge Boulevard (OpenStreetMap).
Pine Avenue and Hazel Avenue are not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
100 ft. Slight rotation (-3 deg): Prospect Ridge Blvd to Hazel Av, Glenview to Bellmawr; platted lots, little built.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 covers the western, newly laid-out part of Haddon Heights between Hillside and Haverford Avenues at the top of the page and the Black Horse Pike, the boundary with the Borough of Mt. Ephraim, at the bottom. The sheet is turned on the page, with north pointing to the left, so the avenues that run north and south on the ground run across the sheet. Five long blocks are drawn between South Park Avenue on the left and Maple Avenue on the right, crossed by St. Martins and Wynnefield Avenues, with Prospect Ridge Boulevard, Sycamore and West High Street running down the page between them. The blocks are subdivided into narrow numbered building lots, most of them still vacant in 1927; the houses that stand are scattered frame dwellings with a few brick-veneered and concrete-block buildings, private garages and a small number of stores near the Black Horse Pike. A filling station with a garage stands on the pike at the foot of South Park Avenue. Beyond Maple Avenue the right side of the sheet shows a large unsubdivided tract with Oak Avenue running diagonally across its upper corner to Glenview Avenue, and the North Branch of Timber Creek at the lower right, which marks the line with the Borough of Bellmawr. Hillside Avenue at the top is marked not opened. Water mains of 4 and 6 inches are shown in most streets, with hydrants at the corners. Glover and Thompson Avenues are lettered beyond the pike, in the area of sheet 20 of the Mt. Ephraim series, which is not drawn here. Block numbers are given with older numbers in parentheses.
notes: Drawn with north to the left of the page (fitted rotation about -71 degrees).
Sycamore is today Sycamore Street and West High is West High Street (OpenStreetMap).
Hillside Avenue is marked not opened.
100 ft, turned with north to the left. Haverford to Black Horse Pike, S. Park to Maple Av; pilot sheet.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 covers the southwestern corner of Haddon Heights, between the Black Horse Pike at the foot of the page, the boundary with the Borough of Mt. Ephraim, and the lake and Hillside Avenue at the top. The sheet is turned on the page, like sheet 14, with north toward the left, so that the avenues running north and south on the ground run across the page. Haverford, St. Martins and Wynnefield Avenues are the long streets running down the page from the lake to the pike; S. Park, Bryn Mawr, Narberth, Wayne and New Jersey Avenues cross them. The blocks, numbered 101 to 120 with older numbers in parentheses, are subdivided into narrow lots and only partly built, with frame dwellings concentrated along Bryn Mawr and Narberth Avenues below Wynnefield and along Wayne Avenue; a larger pink brick dwelling stands on block 103 and a few buildings stand beside Kings Highway at the left. At the top a lake, with the South Branch of Newton Creek entering it from the upper right, lies beside Hillside Avenue, which is marked not opened. Kings Highway runs obliquely down the left side on the line with the Borough of Audubon at the top and the Borough of Mt. Ephraim below, and New Jersey Avenue on the left is also lettered as a borough limit. Bell Road and White Avenue appear beside the pike beyond the sheet's own area. Water mains of 4, 6 and 12 inches are shown in the streets. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Drawn with north toward the left of the page (fitted rotation about -71 degrees).
Hillside Avenue is marked not opened.
Kings Highway runs on the borough line with Audubon and Mt. Ephraim.
100 ft. Turned, north to the left, like 14: Haverford to Black Horse Pike, S. Park to New Jersey Av; lake and Hillside Av (not opened) at top. Kings Highway left out.
